title: Risi e Bisi
subtitle: Venetian pea and rice soup-risotto
excerpt: Risi e bisi is the Venetian spring dish that sits between a risotto and a thick soup: wetter and looser than a standard risotto, made with peas and their pods, and finished with parmesan and butter. Traditionally served on St Mark's Day, 25 April.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risi e bisi is a Venetian dish whose name simply means rice and peas. It was traditionally presented to the Doge of Venice on the feast of St Mark (25 April), when the first spring peas arrived. The dish is wetter than a risotto, almost a thick minestrone, and the pea pods are used to enrich the stock.

content.text: Risi e bisi is not quite a risotto and not quite a soup. It should be loose enough to eat with a spoon but thick enough that the rice does not sink to the bottom. Fresh peas are traditional; the pods go into the stock to add sweetness. Frozen peas work well outside spring and do not need the pod trick.
Heat 1 tablespoon of butter and the olive oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Add the lardons and cook for 3 minutes until beginning to colour. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the rice and stir to coat for 2 minutes. Pour in all the hot stock at once (unlike a standard risotto, risi e bisi uses the absorption method with all the stock). Bring to a simmer.

Cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the peas and cook for 5 more minutes until the rice is tender and the dish is thick but still pourable. It should be looser than a risotto.

Remove from the heat. Add the remaining butter, the parmesan, and the parsley. Stir vigorously. Season with salt and pepper. Serve in warm bowls; it thickens as it sits so bring it quickly to the table.
